**Prepared:** October 26, 2026 · **Privileged & confidential — attorney work product**

Scope: assessment of claims, strengths/weaknesses, contract requirements, and forum, based solely on the
client file (`documents/`) and the closed reference library (`library/`). Assumptions are flagged; open
questions are in `deliverable/QUESTIONS.md`.

## 1. The contract — what it requires

| Provision | What it requires / gives us |
|---|---|

| §7 Entire Agreement | Integration clause — informal statements outside the writing are vulnerable; but §3 expressly contemplates written waivers, so the Feb. 11 email operates inside the contract. |
| Exhibit C.1 | **AAA arbitration, single arbitrator, Capital City, Columbia** — all disputes "including… the arbitrability of any claim" (delegation clause). C.2 class waiver. ## 2. Claim-by-claim assessment

### A. Unpaid invoices — $340,000 · **STRONG (with one invoice contested)**

Per `documents/open_invoices.csv`:

| Invoice | Period | Amount | Due | Dispute notice | Status under §2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| J-4411 | Mar | $68,400 | 2026-04-30 | none | **Deemed accepted** |
| J-4452 | Apr | $71,250 | 2026-05-31 | none | **Deemed accepted** |
| J-4490 | May | $66,100 | 2026-06-30 | none | **Deemed accepted** |
| J-4533 | Jun | $74,800 | 2026-07-31 | yes — 2026-07-09 | timely disputed (see below) |
| J-4571 | Jul | $59,450 | 2026-08-31 | none | **Deemed accepted** |

Priya S. (RN, Apr), Luis F. (RN, May), Keisha B. (LPN, May), Anne O. (RN, Jun), Victor H. (CNA, Jun).
All occurred during the term; §3 applies. None paid fees.

| Hires | Fee at $16k avg | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Rosa M., Tay W. | $32,000 | **Waived — do not demand.** Bell's Feb. 11 email ("consider the fee waived for Rosa and Tay as a one-off") satisfies §3's writing requirement. Asserting these fees would contradict our own file; Pinecrest holds the email. |

of term that "does not extend to later hires" under `library/columbia_account_stated_waiver.md`.

   of contract)" — *Ashby v. Caldera Partners*, 212 Col. App. 3d 440 (2019) (`library/columbia_tortious_interference.md`).

  arbitration and, under Exhibit C.3 plus *Zuniga v. Mercer*, 198 Col. 2d 77 (2017), "a party that files suit
  on arbitrable claims may be compelled to arbitrate and, under a fee clause, may owe the fees of the motion
  to compel" (`library/faa_2_4.md`, `library/fee_shifting_and_candor.md`).
- **No usable court carve-out.** C.6 allows small claims only for "claims solely for collection of undisputed
  invoices of less than $25,000." Every invoice exceeds $25,000 individually, and our claim includes
  conversion fees — so C.6 is unavailable. C.4 (provisional injunction in aid of arbitration) has no obvious
  application here; there is no imminent-irreparable-harm fact pattern.

  cannot move out of arbitration either; fees provisions cut both ways, so pick claims we can win.
  Fee exposure quantification is deferred to Session 5 (no AAA fee data in the library — do not invent one).

## 4. Numbers — showing the arithmetic

**Interest** (contract §2: 1%/month, simple, whole months past due through Oct. 31, 2026 — assumption:
months counted from due date; exact day-count would change figures slightly):

| Invoice | Amount | Due | Months past due | Interest |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| J-4411 | $68,400 | 4/30 | 6 | $4,104.00 |
| J-4452 | $71,250 | 5/31 | 5 | $3,562.50 |
| J-4490 | $66,100 | 6/30 | 4 | $2,644.00 |
| J-4533 | $74,800 | 7/31 | 3 | $2,244.00 |
| J-4571 | $59,450 | 8/31 | 2 | $1,189.00 |
| | **$340,000** | | | **$13,743.50** |

**Conversion fees (CEO average $64,000):** 0.25 × $64,000 = $16,000/hire.
Clean (2 hires) = $32,000 · contested (3 hires) = $48,000 · waived (2 hires) = $32,000.

**Defensible demand:** $340,000 + $13,743.50 + $80,000 (5 non-waived hires) = **$433,743.50**.

**Reconciliation with the CEO's $862,000** (it does not survive intact, and here is exactly where the gap is):

```
$862,000 (CEO) = $433,743.50 (defensible demand)
               + $410,000   tortious interference — do not assert (§2C above)
               + $32,000    Rosa & Tay conversion fees — waived in writing by our own account manager
               − $13,743.50 contractual interest we now add
Check: 433,743.50 + 410,000 + 32,000 − 13,743.50 = 862,000.00 ✓
```

If Pinecrest substantiates J-4533 "padding" and wins the course-of-dealing argument on Priya/Luis/Keisha,
the realistic floor is ~$356,699.50 ($265,200 + $11,499.50 + $80,000 conversion claims are partial-risk;
$32,000 of those conversion fees are clean → hard floor ≈ $308,699.50–$356,699.50 depending on J-4533).
Settlement banding is a Session 5 exercise; these are ranges, not promises.

## 5. Strengths / weaknesses summary

**Strengths:** deemed-accepted invoices under §2 + account stated (CJI 14.02) on $265,200; contractual
1%/month interest; §3 fee clause with a waiver written "as a one-off" that by its terms does not extend
further; §6 carve-out expressly preserves fees and conversion fees; J-4533 challenge has produced nothing
since July; corporate cost-cutting was Pinecrest's stated reason, which frames the hires as business as
usual rather than our management.

**Weaknesses:** the Feb. 11 waiver email kills $32,000 of the fee claim and colors the next three hires;
Bell's equivocal texts ("ha, we'll talk", "call me") create a fact-finder waiver/estoppel risk worth ~$48,000;
the tortious-interference claim is the CEO's favorite number ($410,000) and the least defensible piece of
the case; the arbitration clause forces us into a forum where C.3 fee-shifting can penalize a wrong first
move; conversion-fee amounts rest on an unverified $64,000 average, and per-hire compensation (RN vs. CNA
mix) could move the number materially in either direction.

**Candor note (per CONTRACT.md standards):** the file we hold contradicts a large share of the CEO's
$862,000. The demand letter asserts $433,743.50 and stays off the tort theory entirely. Per
`library/fee_shifting_and_candor.md`, a misstatement in a demand letter that is repeated in a pleading
becomes a statement to a tribunal — so the letter is built only on what the file can prove.

Agreement between Juniper and Pinecrest Senior Living, Inc. ("Pinecrest") effective January 15, 2024

correspondence. This letter states Juniper's position and demand, and it is written in the hope of
resolving this matter without arbitration.

## 1. Unpaid invoices — $340,000

|---|---|---|---|---|
| J-4411 | March 2026 | $68,400.00 | Apr. 30, 2026 | Not disputed within 15 days — deemed accepted |

noticed within 15 days of receipt, and provides that invoices not timely disputed "are deemed accepted."

they are, in addition, an account stated. Payment of those four invoices — **$265,200.00** — is past due
and is demanded in full.

has received no audit findings, no identification of the shifts said to be padded, and no credit memo.

time records within the response period below; Juniper will credit any verified overcharge, and nothing
else. Absent that substantiation, J-4533 must be paid in full.

## 2. Contractual interest

Section 2 provides that late amounts "bear interest at 1% per month." Interest accrued through
October 31, 2026 is **$13,743.50**, and continues to accrue:

| Invoice | Amount × 1%/month × months past due (through Oct. 31, 2026) | Interest |
|---|---|---|
| J-4411 | $68,400.00 × 1% × 6 | $4,104.00 |
| J-4452 | $71,250.00 × 1% × 5 | $3,562.50 |
| J-4490 | $66,100.00 × 1% × 4 | $2,644.00 |

| J-4571 | $59,450.00 × 1% × 2 | $1,189.00 |
| **Total** | | **$13,743.50** |

## 3. Conversion fees — five hires

Section 3 provides that Pinecrest shall not directly hire Personnel introduced by Juniper during the term
(and for 12 months thereafter) "except upon payment of a conversion fee equal to 25% of the Personnel's
first-year annualized compensation." Between March and June 2026, Pinecrest hired seven Juniper personnel.

Juniper is not asserting conversion fees for **Rosa M. and Tay W.** In an email dated February 11, 2026,
Juniper's account manager waived the fee for those two hires. That waiver was honored, and by its own terms
it was "a one-off" — it did not extend to anyone else, and Section 3 permits waivers only in writing.

No written waiver exists for the remaining five hires, each of whom Pinecrest hired without payment of any
conversion fee:

| Hire | Role | Month hired | Conversion fee due |
|---|---|---|---|
| Priya S. | RN | April 2026 | $16,000.00 |
| Luis F. | RN | May 2026 | $16,000.00 |
| Keisha B. | LPN | May 2026 | $16,000.00 |
| Anne O. | RN | June 2026 | $16,000.00 |
| Victor H. | CNA | June 2026 | $16,000.00 |
| **Total** | | | **$80,000.00** |

Each figure is 25% × $64,000, the average first-year annualized compensation for this group based on the
information currently available to Juniper. These amounts are stated as minimums: the fee is calculated
hire by hire, and Juniper reserves the right to adjust each figure upon production of actual first-year
compensation data, including from Pinecrest's own payroll records.

To be clear about the record: Pinecrest announced each of these hires to Juniper in advance. Juniper's
informal responses to those announcements were not — and under Section 3 could not be — waivers, which the
Agreement requires in writing. Pinecrest's stated reason for the hires was a corporate mandate to reduce
agency spend, which does not relieve it of the fee that Section 3 attaches to exactly this decision.

## 4. Total demand

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Unpaid invoices (J-4411, J-4452, J-4490, J-4533, J-4571) | $340,000.00 |
| Contractual interest through Oct. 31, 2026 | $13,743.50 |

| **Total demanded through Oct. 31, 2026** | **$433,743.50** |

plus interest accruing at 1% per month thereafter on unpaid amounts, and Juniper's costs and fees to the
extent provided by Exhibit C.3.

## 5. Forum and next steps

Exhibit C.1 of the Agreement requires that any dispute arising out of or relating to it — including
arbitrability — be resolved exclusively by binding arbitration before a single arbitrator under the AAA
Commercial Arbitration Rules in Capital City, Columbia. Exhibit C.3 entitles the prevailing party in any
arbitration, or in any action to compel arbitration, to recover its reasonable attorneys' fees and costs.
Juniper has no interest in the parties paying each other's fees over claims as straightforward as these,
and it will not be filing court litigation that its own contract prohibits.

**Demand:** payment of **$433,743.50**, or a substantive written response — including the June audit
findings for J-4533 and a proposal on the conversion fees — within **fourteen (14) days** of this letter,
i.e., by **November 9, 2026**. If the matter is not resolved by that date, Juniper will file a demand for
arbitration with the American Arbitration Association seeking all of the amounts above, accruing interest,
and fees and costs under Exhibit C.3.

This letter is written to facilitate resolution; it is not a waiver of any right or remedy under the
Agreement or applicable law, all of which are reserved.

Very truly yours,

**[Name]**
Outside Counsel for Juniper Health Staffing, LLC

cc: Dolapo Okonkwo, Chief Executive Officer, Juniper Health Staffing, LLC
